title: Land Acquisition Compensation Law in Bangladesh
metaTitle: Land Acquisition Compensation Law in Bangladesh
metaDescription: Guide to land acquisition compensation under the Acquisition Act 2017 in Bangladesh, covering the 200% statutory premium, DC objections, and arbitration.
heroIntro: Under Sections 8 and 9 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act 2017, private landowners in Bangladesh receive assessed market value plus a 200% statutory compensation premium for public projects, or 300% for private-entity projects. Owners can contest acquisition necessity and low valuation before the DC and Arbitrator.

sections.title: Legal Framework Under the 2017 Acquisition Act
sections.content:
Compulsory acquisition of private land in Bangladesh is governed by the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act 2017, replacing the 1982 Ordinance and protecting property rights under Constitution Article 42(2). Before any government ministry, road authority, or utility agency can take possession, the Deputy Commissioner (DC) must prove public necessity and serve sequential statutory notices upon recorded proprietors.

Under Section 4, the DC issues a preliminary notice posted in visible public places and delivered to owners appearing in updated mutation and settlement khatians. Affected owners hold an enforceable right under Section 5 to lodge formal written objections within fifteen working days challenging necessity, road alignment, or exclusion of homestead and religious structures. Failing to file timely objections lets proceedings move straight toward Section 7 final notice.

Prior to disbursement, owners facing co-sharer disputes should settle co-sharer partition claims and verify their online e-Namjari mutation record. Unlawful eviction bypassing valid Section 7 notices can be halted via High Court writ petitions.

sections.title: How Market Value and 200% Compensation Are Calculated
sections.content:
Section 9 of the 2017 Act obligates the Deputy Commissioner to compute base land value from the twelve-month average of registered mouza sale deeds, plus mandatory statutory premiums. Beyond raw land valuation, PWD engineers and Forest appraisers separately assess brick buildings, boundary walls, ponds, standing crops, and fruit trees under Section 9(1).

Lawmakers enacted the 2017 statute specifically to triple the old solatium and counteract artificially understated deed values recorded at Sub-Registry offices. For government ministries or statutory agencies, Section 9(2) adds an extra 200% above market price (yielding 300% total compensation). For private-company projects approved for public benefit, Section 9(3) mandates an extra 300% premium (400% total).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Procedure from Section 4 Notice to Award
sections.content:
Collecting acquisition awards demands clearing every ownership query between the Section 4 preliminary notice and Section 11 cheque disbursement at the District LA Branch. Unmutated ancestral CS, SA, RS, or BS khatians frequently freeze funds in treasury custody:

  1. Inspect Section 4 Notice & File Section 5 Objection: Record the LA Case Number immediately, match notified dag numbers against your deed, and submit a written Section 5 objection within fifteen working days if homesteads or mosques are affected.
  2. Attend Joint Field Survey & Structure Valuation: Remain physically present when surveyors and PWD engineers measure rooms, concrete roofs, boundary walls, utilities, and trees for the joint inventory list.
  3. Submit Title Chain Under Sections 7 & 8 Notices: Appear before the LA Officer with original deeds, 25-year chain deeds, mutation khatian, and updated rent dakhilas to establish uncontested ownership for your Section 8 Award.
  4. Accept Section 11 Cheque Under Protest if Undervalued: Collect account-payee payment—explicitly writing "received under protest" if seeking enhancement.

Partial acquisitions blocking road frontage may also preserve statutory easement access rights across retained plots.

sections.title: Required Documents to Claim Full Acquisition Award
sections.content:
District LA Officers rigorously verify the continuous 25-year chain of title from historical CS/RS/BS khatians down to the present claimant before signing Section 11 compensation vouchers. Minor mismatches in mouza schedules, dag splits, or parent spelling halt payment indefinitely inside contested deposit accounts:

  • Original registered Saf Kabla, Heba gift deed, or civil decree alongside certified bia chain deeds tracing 25 years of possession.
  • Updated e-Namjari mutation khatian, official DCR receipt, and current Land Development Tax (Khajna) dakhila receipts.
  • Original Section 4, Section 7, and Section 8 LA Case notices served by the Deputy Commissioner's office bearing schedule details.
  • National ID card (NID), active TIN certificate, bank routing cheque leaf copy, and recent attested passport photographs.
  • City Corporation or Union Parishad Warish certificate plus notarized co-heir consent deeds where inheriting ancestral property.
  • Sub-Registry non-encumbrance search certificate confirming the acquired schedule is free from bank mortgages or pending civil attachments.

NRBs unable to travel may execute an embassy-attested Power of Attorney or order remote land title vetting beforehand.

sections.title: Challenging Low Compensation & NRB Representation
sections.content:
Owners awarded undervalued compensation may petition within forty-five days under Section 28 of the 2017 Act for judicial reference to an Arbitrator—provided payment was collected under protest. Before a Joint District Judge Arbitrator, independent adjacent commercial sale deeds, PWD structure valuations, and business severance records routinely secure substantial awards plus Section 34 statutory interest.

Rival ownership claims inside the LA Branch are referred to civil adjudication under Section 30 before funds are disbursed, whereas illegal notices bypassing Section 4 or targeting exempt burial grounds can be stayed through a High Court Writ Petition under Article 102.

faqs.question: How much compensation does a landowner get for land acquisition in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 9 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act 2017, private owners receive assessed market value plus a 200% statutory premium (300% total) for public agencies, and +300% (400% total) for private-entity projects, plus separate compensation for buildings, crops, and trees.

faqs.question: What is the deadline to object to a Section 4 acquisition notice?
faqs.answer: Under Section 5 of the 2017 Act, interested landowners must file written objections with the Deputy Commissioner within fifteen working days of Section 4 notice service. Missing this window forfeits administrative objections unless exceptional illegality justifies High Court writ intervention.

faqs.question: Can I challenge low valuation after accepting the DC payment cheque?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided you explicitly signed 'under protest' when collecting the Section 11 cheque. Under Section 28 of the 2017 Act, you must submit a written reference petition within forty-five days asking the Deputy Commissioner to forward the dispute to the Arbitrator.

faqs.question: What happens if acquired land lacks updated mutation in my name?
faqs.answer: The LA Officer requires valid mutation and updated land tax receipts before issuing payment. When mutation is incomplete or heirs dispute shares, the DC deposits funds into treasury custody under Section 30 until claimants produce civil title clearance confirming exact ownership.

faqs.question: Can NRB owners claim acquisition compensation without visiting Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Non-resident Bangladeshis can execute a Special Power of Attorney attested by the Bangladesh Embassy abroad and verified by MOFA in Dhaka, authorizing a family member or advocate to clear LA verification, file Section 28 references, and receive compensation.
